canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. The available paper treats sentence classification as a task of categorizing sentences by syntactic structure, with labels such as simple, complex, compound, and compound-complex. Success is described as producing "a list of correctly classified sentences with labels" (Automated Knowledge Graph Construction using Large Language Models and Sentence Complexity Modelling).

Variants. The described task scope centers on classifying among sentence types, specifically simple, complex, compound, and compound-complex. No other sub-tasks, domains, modalities, or alternative names are described.

Space of elicitation and scores. No measurement instrument is linked to it. The available paper describes model-based evaluation, noting that transformer-based models and smaller LLMs were fine-tuned on a training set and evaluated on a test set for sentence types, but no named instrument is recorded as eliciting or scoring the behavior.

What it is taken as evidence of. No construct is linked to it as what this behavior indicates, so the available relationships do not specify any broader construct that sentence classification is taken to evidence.
